Your car and your home are your most important assets, yet the experience of owning them is stuck in the 90s. Every part of the journey - insurance, repairs, financing, maintenance - is fragmented, complicated, and expensive. Jerry is building the first app to manage it all.

Why We're Hiring
The next frontier is helping people with the cost of owning a home. Property tax appeals is one of the first offerings we're building - and the Florida appeals season is starting.
This is a domain where being 90% right isn’t going to cut it. Florida's Value Adjustment Board process has a 25-day filing window, a partial-payment requirement that silently kills otherwise-valid petitions, and 67 counties that each run the process differently. Before a single homeowner's petition depends on what we build, we need someone who has lived inside that system to pressure-test it.
This is a deliberately narrow engagement - a few hours a week from someone excellent. The work is advisory: reviewing what we build, flagging what won't survive contact with the VAB, and telling us when we're wrong before it costs a customer.

• Hourly, as-needed : This is an independent contractor engagement at roughly 5-10 hours per week with no fixed schedule. If this product starts to see traction, there is a path to a full-time permanent role if you’re interested.

• Early-stage product : You are advising on a new product. The customer flows, backend authorization flows, and filing logic is still being shaped. Your job is to help guide our design and help correct things before we push it to production.

• Regulatory grounding : Clarify how things like Chapter 194, F.S. and the DOR uniform rules (12D-9, 12D-10) operate in practice and not only how they read on paper.

• County-level reality : Walk us through how the Property Appraiser's offices and VABs actually differ across the volume counties: Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach, Hillsborough, Orange, Duval, Pinellas, and Lee.

• Filing mechanics : TRIM notice timing, the 25-day window, DR-486 and its variants, e-filing versus paper, and the §194.014 partial-payment requirement - guide us through the process.

• Hearings and evidence : Help build a flow that actually wins in front of a special magistrate - comparable selection, the 15-day and 7-day evidence exchange windows, and condition-based arguments.

Who You Are

• Built inside the VAB system : You can describe why Broward is different from Hillsborough without looking it up. Your knowledge was built through filings or arguing petitions, not advising on property tax from a distance.

• Volume-tested : You've worked across hundreds of parcels and seen enough edge cases that you recognize the pattern before it becomes a problem.

• Procedurally sharp : You know every step of the appeals process as if it was the back of your hand.

What You'll Bring

• 5+ years of direct, hands-on Florida experience filing residential property tax appeals.

• Personal experience filing or arguing petitions before a Florida VAB, or adjudicating them as a special magistrate.

• No active conflict: not currently advising another company building consumer property tax appeal software.

• Florida-based strongly preferred, given county-level familiarity requirements.

Litigation involving religious liberty, state action, labor law, school funding, civil rights, and constitutional structure will shape the future of the charter movement for decades. The National Alliance seeks an experienced litigator and strategic thinker to help identify emerging legal threats before they become crises and develop national litigation strategies that protect and strengthen public charter schools.

Reporting to the Chief Legal Officer and working collaboratively with other senior attorneys, the Vice President will be relied upon to lead many of our legal programs. This role combines elements of a wide variety of activities, including strategic issue identification, litigation strategy and management, coalition building, communications, and network development. What You'll Do

• Engage in federal and state litigation to protect charter schools as public schools.

• Work in partnership with local advocates on case theory and strategy, reviewing and editing briefs and offering guidance based on other charter cases.

• Coordinate with the communications function at the National Alliance to develop media strategies.

• Recruit potential litigants (plaintiffs and defendant intervenors).

• Identify and vet cases to prevent encroachments on, or make advances in, charter school autonomy and funding access policies.

• Expand the movement's legal capability by cultivating the growth and development of our legal network (the Alliance of Public Charter School Attorneys) and leveraging the experience and expertise it provides.

• Develop in-person and virtual trainings to support network learning and find and cultivate new attorneys for the network, especially in high-need areas.

• Network and speak on key issues to advance the legal advocacy agenda.

• Monitor legal cases filed around the country and identify potential federal and multi-state legal policy issues that may adversely impact the charter sector or present new opportunities.

Who You Are

• You have experience with media and leveraging communications as part of a litigation advocacy campaign.

title: Manufacturing Engineer
description:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO

- Build the machine that builds the machine. Join TechOps at the forefront of advanced manufacturing, we’re building the production system that will enable commercial fusion. The Production lines, tooling, and processes are being developed from the ground up; you'll create the ways of working, not inherit them.

- Work at the frontier of manufacturing technology. Bring your creativity to evaluate, qualify, and deploy processes with no industry playbook, every component you build and every process you shape goes directly into the core of the stellarator magnet technology.

- Do work that matters, and see it grow. The hardware you build is the product and your career grows with it, from prototyping and process development through quality and industrialization, alongside exceptional colleagues from around the world.

- Make an impact you can point to. In a small, fast-moving team, your calls on equipment, quality, and process directly shape how a world-class deep-tech company produces superconducting magnets with results visible on the shop floor, not buried in a slidedeck.

YOUR IMPACT

Develop and industrialize the manufacturing processes used to build HTS magnet coils.

Translate magnet designs into repeatable, high-yield production processes in collaboration with design, physics, and production teams.

Own the tooling, fixtures, and quality systems required to deliver consistent and reliable manufacturing outcomes.

Lead process development from prototype builds through the transition to full-scale manufacturing.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Develop, qualify, and continuously improve manufacturing processes for HTS coil winding, insulation, impregnation, and joining, working closely with magnet design and materials engineers.

- Drive design-for-manufacturing/design-for-assembly (DFM (Design for Manufacturing)/DFA (Design for Assembly)) collaboration with the design team, acting as the manufacturing voice in design reviews to keep coil designs buildable, scalable, and serviceable.

- Design, procure, and validate tooling, fixtures, and jigs for precision winding and assembly of non-planar coil geometries, including capability studies where needed.

- Define assembly sequences, work instructions, SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures), and visual aids for technicians, and maintain this documentation as designs evolve.

- Define and implement process controls and inspection methods (dimensional, electrical, structural) to catch defects early and protect conductor integrity.

- Lead NPI (New Product Introduction) campaigns, process trials and pilot builds, and provide hands-on floor support during prototype and early production builds.

- Lead root-cause analysis and corrective actions (8D (Eight Disciplines problem-solving methodology), 5-Why, fishbone, etc.) for yield, quality, and cycle-time issues, and apply Lean/Six Sigma principles to drive measurable process improvement.

You are the connective tissue across compute, network, storage, power, and cooling. • Proven large-scale incident command experience and calm technical leadership on a bridge.

• Demonstrated monitoring and observability design at fleet or campus scale, including alert hygiene, suppression, and signal quality.

• Experience working across at least two of: compute, network, storage, power, and cooling / facilities telemetry.

• Excellent problem-solving skills with a data-driven approach to reliability engineering.

• Ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams, including NOC, data center operations, and infrastructure engineering.

• Experience in AI/ML infrastructure or supercomputing environments.

• Hands-on definition and use of SLOs, SLIs, and error budgets at service or campus boundaries.

• Experience running game days, dependency mapping, and closed-loop corrective action programs.

• Familiarity with data center hardware and plant signals (servers, GPUs, networking, power, cooling) in addition to software telemetry.

• Prior work in a fast-paced startup or tech company like SpaceXAI.
